runtimeScope: Capture the bounded requested quantity/note in ambiguous update-item receipts, including omitted or invalid indices with multiple owners. A source-proven retry resolves a missing-owner rejection.

Persist one unambiguous update/remove proposal with all completely accepted purchases, source text, candidate cart rows, cart signature, relevant catalog fingerprint, page and expiry in optional pendingReplacementClarification.ownerChoice.
Show the proposed final quantity or complete note and every new purchase before asking one owner question. Apply the selected row and all retained purchases atomically without another model call.

Validate cart/catalog/availability/expiry and current business hours, reapply action guards and purchase/limit checks, preserve the original session on partial failure and clear the marker only after committing the complete plan.

Handle numeric and exact current-option/note choices, spoken numbers, pagination, JSON persistence, repeated replies, cancellation, restart, intermediate read-only queries and fresh complete reformulations.
Defer to another active cart/catalog/contact/location choice and invalidate the stale proposal. Signed replies and menu codes retain distinct interpretation.

Backend-owned cartEditOwnerRecovery re-enters the agent only for a fresh named customer request. Its contract requires one source-proven edit of the same type and all named pending purchases before the shared atomic commit, including during checkout.
developmentFindings: All four initial numeric recovery cases failed because the previous source had no persisted owner choice.

The initial extended pending-attribute fixture omitted materialized name/code/price/attribute fields. It was corrected before final validation. Spoken list numbers now reuse the catalog quantity vocabulary with its unit context.

A signed numeric reply was normalized to a positive row and mutated the simulated cart. Raw signed-prefix handling now protects negative, polite and Unicode forms. A menu-code regression protects code/list ownership.

An external normal-entry probe found that a fresh complete request after price invalidation could be partially applied while retaining its old blocker. The development global was interrupted, and backend-owned full-plan recovery now validates and commits that request as a whole.

The final recovery checks preserve closed-hour restrictions, failed or omitted purchases, current notes, order review, another active option/location dialogue and the existing product-conversion entry. The ordinary final-order price-refresh and reconfirmation behavior is reused.
limits: Provider responses, Meta, persistence, map quotes and order creation are simulated. Real-model wording and representative pilot outcomes require further measurement.

The selector covers one stable update/remove proposal for an existing SKU with multiple current variants. Rejected replacements, incompatible edit payloads and other mixed actions retain their full-request clarification.

Fresh reformulation recovery requires the source and pending purchases to be fully named, the same edit type and complete accepted tool evidence. Partial revocation of purchases and broader cross-tool plan recovery require further work.
Existing product conversions keep their normal entry. More regional aliases, group-of-lines requests and source/delivery nomenclature overlaps need additional cases.
